subject_name.description: Only needed when no canonical title was given: the main entity the passage is about.

subject_context.description: One short clause naming what kind of thing this is, in the source's own words, e.g. 'a football stadium in Petah Tikva, Israel'. This is the context a reader needs before any single fact makes sense.

context_tags.description: General category phrases this subject shares with OTHER subjects, e.g. 'football stadium'. Common nouns only - never a proper name.

no_new_information.description: True only when every fact in the passage is already in the 'Already recorded' list. Never true because you personally recognize the subject.

new_facts.description: The facts the passage states about the subject, each carrying the context that makes it meaningful on its own.

relation.description: Snake_case verb built from a verb written near the object in the source, e.g. 'located_in', 'completed_in'.

context.description: The situating clause a later reader needs, in a few words.

evidence_quote.description: The verbatim source fragment that states this fact.
